steps.title: Design DNA nanomachine (DNM)
steps.instruction: Design the DNM targeting a unique 16S rRNA region using UNAFold and DINAMelt, construct Dza, T1 and T2 strands with appropriate arms and tile, verify secondary structures, draw schematic and order oligos.

substeps.instruction: Select a unique genomic region or SNV‑containing region of the target 16S rRNA using BLAST.
Open UNAFold (mFold tab), paste the target sequence, set folding temperature to 55 °C, ionic conditions to [Mg++] = 200 mM and [Na+] = 215 mM, keep all other parameters default, and click “Fold DNA”.
Choose a stable hairpin where the DNM binding site lies in an unstructured region or loop.

If the target site is in a stem‑loop, design Arm 2 to bind one side of the stem, the loop and 3–5 nt of the opposite side (center the SNV in Arm 2 for selectivity) and design Arm 3 to bind the opposite side of the stem.

Calculate melting temperatures (Tm) using UNAFold DINAMelt (Two‑State Melting): set DNA at 55 °C, [Na+] = 215 mM, [Mg++] = 100 mM, strand concentration = 0.02 µM. Ensure Tm(Arm 2) ≥ 56–58 °C and Tm(Arm 1, 3, 4) > 65 °C.
Assemble Dza strand: 5′‑Arm 2‑[half of 10‑23 core]‑F‑sub (or Cy‑sub)‑3′.
Check Dza secondary structure on UNAFold; ΔG must be ≥ ‑4 kcal/mol and avoid long GC‑rich stretches.
Assemble T1 strand: 5′‑F‑sub (or Cy‑sub)‑[second half of 10‑23 core]‑Arm 3‑HEG‑tile‑3′. Use provided tile sequence or a random sequence of equal length; tile Tm > 65 °C, low GC bias.
Check T1 secondary structure on UNAFold; ΔG ≥ ‑4 kcal/mol. If too stable, introduce point mutations toward arm ends.
Assemble T2 strand: 5′‑Arm 1‑HEG‑complementary tile of T1‑HEG‑Arm 4‑3′.
Check T2 secondary structure on UNAFold; ΔG ≥ ‑4 kcal/mol. If needed, mutate Arms 1/4 or shift them 2–3 nt away from Arms 2/3.
Draw the complete DNM (all four strands) in a vector graphics program, confirming 5′→3′ orientation.
Order all oligonucleotides from a commercial vendor (stock solutions at 100 µM, to be diluted with nuclease‑free water).

steps.title: Assemble DNM strands and verify by PAGE
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 µM oligo stocks, thaw, assemble 1 µM DNM aliquots for B. thuringiensis and B. mycoides, heat‑shock, run a 12 % native PAGE, stain with ethidium bromide and image.

substeps.instruction: Dilute each lyophilized oligo (T1_thu, T2_thu, T1_myc, T2_myc) to 10 µM in nuclease‑free water; store at ‑20 °C.
Thaw the 10 µM solutions, tap gently to mix, spin briefly in a microcentrifuge.

In separate 1.5 mL tubes, combine the appropriate T1 and T2 strands with nuclease‑free water to obtain 1 µM final concentration for the B. thuringiensis‑specific DNM (see Recipes) and for the B. mycoides‑specific DNM.
Gently mix each tube, spin down, and seal the lids with parafilm (or use screw‑cap tubes).
Place the sealed tubes in a 500 mL beaker containing boiling water for 2 min, then turn off the heater and allow the tubes to cool to room temperature overnight.
Prepare a 12 % native PAGE: mix 1 mL 10× TBE, 3 mL 40 % AA:BA, add MQ water to 10 mL, then add 50 µL 10 % APS and 5 µL TEMED; pour into a gel cassette and let polymerize.
Add 1 µL of each sample (assembled DNM and each individual component) to 1 µL 4× loading dye, then load the mixtures into separate wells.
Run the gel at 80 V for 90 min in 1× TBE buffer.
Stain the gel with ethidium bromide and visualize bands using a gel‑documentation system.

steps.title: Characterize DNM activity with synthetic analytes
steps.instruction: Test DNM catalytic activity using 200 nM fluorescent substrates (F‑sub for B. thuringiensis, Cy‑sub for B. mycoides) with serial analyte concentrations, incubate at 55 °C for 1 h, and record fluorescence.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 160 µL of 200 nM F‑sub in Col buffer (background substrate control).
Make seven 160 µL reaction tubes each containing 20 nM B. thuringiensis‑specific DNM, 20 nM B. thuringiensis‑specific Dza, and 200 nM F‑sub in reaction buffer. Keep tube 1 as blank.
Add B. thuringiensis synthetic analyte to tubes 2–7 to reach final concentrations of 1, 10, 100, 200, 500 and 1 000 pM.
Gently mix, spin down, and split each tube into three 50 µL aliquots placed in a black 96‑well plate.
Prepare 160 µL of 200 nM Cy‑sub in reaction buffer (background for mycoides).
Repeat the above steps (prepare seven tubes, add mycoides analyte at 1–1 000 pM, split into plate) using 20 nM B. mycoides‑specific DNM, 15 nM B. mycoides‑specific Dza, and Cy‑sub.
Seal the plate with an optically transparent film.
Incubate the sealed plate at 55 °C for 1 h (water bath or heating chamber), then spin down briefly.
Measure fluorescence of the F‑sub wells at 525 nm (excitation = 495 nm); calculate mean ± SD for each analyte concentration.
Measure fluorescence of the Cy‑sub wells at 662 nm (excitation = 617 nm); calculate mean ± SD for each analyte concentration.

steps.title: Extract total RNA from bacterial cultures
steps.instruction: Extract total RNA from B. thuringiensis, B. mycoides and B. cereus cultures using the Oh & So protocol (or any suitable gram‑positive bacterial RNA extraction method) and assess RNA integrity by agarose gel electrophoresis.

steps.title: Detect extracted 16S rRNA using DNM
steps.instruction: Set up fluorescence assays with total RNA (1–10 ng/µL) using the appropriate DNM and fluorescent substrate, incubate at 55 °C for 1 h, and read fluorescence at 525 nm (F‑sub) and 662 nm (Cy‑sub).

substeps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration of each extracted sample at 260 nm.
Prepare 160 µL of 200 nM F‑sub in reaction buffer.
Make nine 160 µL tubes each containing 20 nM B. thuringiensis‑specific DNM, 20 nM B. thuringiensis‑specific Dza and 200 nM F‑sub. Keep tube 1 as blank.
Add B. thuringiensis total RNA to tubes 2–7 to reach final concentrations of 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 ng/µL.
Add B. cereus total RNA (10 ng/µL) to tube 8 and B. mycoides total RNA (10 ng/µL) to tube 9.
Gently mix, spin down, and split each reaction into three 50 µL aliquots in a black 96‑well plate.
Prepare 160 µL of 200 nM Cy‑sub in reaction buffer.
Repeat the above (steps 2‑6) using 20 nM B. mycoides‑specific DNM, 15 nM B. mycoides‑specific Dza, 200 nM Cy‑sub and the same RNA concentration series (1–10 ng/µL for mycoides, 10 ng/µL for cereus).
Seal the plate with an optically transparent film.
Incubate at 55 °C for 1 h, then spin down briefly.
Measure fluorescence of F‑sub wells at 525 nm (excitation = 495 nm); calculate mean ± SD.
Measure fluorescence of Cy‑sub wells at 662 nm (excitation = 617 nm); calculate mean ± SD.

steps.title: Detect 16S rRNA in crude cell lysates
steps.instruction: Prepare serial dilutions of bacterial cultures, lyse cells, add DNM/Dza, heat‑treat, supplement with RNase inhibitor and fluorescent substrate, incubate at 55 °C for 1 h, and record fluorescence at 525 nm and 662 nm.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate 5 mL autoclaved LB broth with each species in separate 15 mL tubes; grow B. thuringiensis and B. cereus at 37 °C, 250 rpm for 16 h, and B. mycoides at 30 °C without shaking for 16 h.
Transfer 1 mL of each culture to a 1.5 mL tube and measure OD₆₀₀.
Dilute each culture with sterile 0.9 % NaCl to OD₆₀₀ = 1 (≈10⁷ CFU/mL for B. thuringiensis, 10⁸ CFU/mL for B. mycoides, 10⁹ CFU/mL for B. cereus).
Create serial dilutions:
• For B. thuringiensis: add 100 µL culture to 900 µL 0.9 % NaCl → 10⁶ CFU/mL, then repeat 10‑fold dilutions down to ~0 CFU/mL.
• For B. mycoides: add 10 µL culture to 990 µL 0.9 % NaCl → 10⁶ CFU/mL, then continue 10‑fold dilutions.
• For B. cereus: add 10 µL culture to 990 µL 0.9 % NaCl → 10⁷ CFU/mL, then dilute to 10⁶ CFU/mL as needed.

Centrifuge each dilution tube at 900 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 160 µL reaction buffer containing 20 nM species‑specific DNM and 20 nM (or 15 nM for mycoides) Dza.
Heat the suspension at 95 °C for 5 min, then let cool at room temperature for 5 min.
Centrifuge again at 900 × g for 3 min; transfer ~150 µL supernatant to a clean tube.
Add 3.75 µL RNase inhibitor (40 U/µL) to achieve 1 U/µL final concentration, then add F‑sub (for B. thuringiensis) or Cy‑sub (for B. mycoides) to a final concentration of 200 nM.

For B. mycoides, repeat the above steps using reaction buffer with 20 nM B. mycoides‑specific DNM, 15 nM Dza, and Cy‑sub. (When testing B. mycoides DNM, use 1 mL of B. thuringiensis culture directly without further dilution, as noted).
Spin down the tubes and incubate at 55 °C for 1 h.
Gently mix, spin down, and divide each reaction into three 50 µL aliquots in a black 96‑well plate.
Measure fluorescence of F‑sub wells at 525 nm (excitation = 495 nm).
Measure fluorescence of Cy‑sub wells at 662 nm (excitation = 617 nm).
